# Data format

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_docs.py from src/wmt26_mteval/schemas.py and data/metadata/lang_codes.tsv. Do not edit by hand. -->

Columns, types and conventions of the configs in `wmt/wmt26-mteval-data`. This file is generated by `scripts/render_docs.py`; the same descriptions are stored in the Parquet files and printed on the dataset card.

## Conventions

### Item identifiers

An `item_id` has six fields joined by the separator `_###_`:

```text
<collection>_###_<source>_###_<target>_###_<domain or set>_###_<document>_###_<para>
official_###_eng_Latn_###_arz_Arab_###_news_###_brisbanetimes.com.au.377415_###_0
```

| field | column | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `collection` | `official` for the main test set, `challenge` for a challenge set. |
| 2, 3 | `src_lang_orig`, `tgt_lang_orig` | The language codes as written in the id; `src_lang` and `tgt_lang` hold the normalised codes. |
| 4 | `domain` or `challenge_set` | The domain of an official item (`news`, `social`, `speech`, `software`, `edu` or `factchecking`), or the name of the challenge set (`GAMBITP`, `FECE`, `QEbreak`, `AGGREE` or `LIGATUR`). The two RefQuality sets keep the domain here and carry their name in the document field. |
| 5 | `doc_id` | The source document. The document of a RefQuality item starts with the name of its set (`RefQuality-PD_` or `RefQuality-PE_`); one that starts with `RefQuality-PD_RefQuality-PE_` marks the pseudo-reference variant of an item whose alternative reference is a post-edit. |
| 6 | `para_idx` | The zero-based paragraph index (see below). |

`para_idx` is null for FECE and QEbreak, whose ids end in a segment hash instead of a paragraph number.

Split on the whole separator, not on `#`: `item_id.split("_###_")`. Document ids can themselves contain `_`, `|` and `.`.

### Language codes

Codes are normalised to an ISO 639-3 language code and an ISO 15924 script, plus a region where one is needed (`eng_Latn`, `zho_Hans`, `zho_Hant_TW`); the original codes stay in `src_lang_orig` and `tgt_lang_orig`. The `lp` column is the paper's short form: the first three letters of each side, except that a Simplified Chinese target is `zho_CN` and Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) is `zho_TW` (`eng-zho_CN`, `eng-zho_TW`, `zho-jpn`).

### Reference types

`ref_type` says how the reference was produced:

| `ref_type` | source data | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `native` | `human` | A human translation from scratch. |
| `postedit` | `postedit` | A post-edited machine translation. |
| `pseudo` | `pseudo` | A machine-generated pseudo-reference. |
| `unknown` | `undefined` | A reference text is present, but the source data does not record its type. |
| `none` | absent, or null text and type | The item has no reference text, and `ref_text` is null. |

`items.ref_type_orig` keeps the type exactly as the source data spells it (`human`, `postedit`, `pseudo`, `undefined`, or null where none is recorded).

### System types

`system_type` classifies the system behind a hypothesis:

| `system_type` | the `system` is |
| --- | --- |
| `mt` | A machine translation system. |
| `human_scratch` | `Human (from scratch)`. |
| `human_postedit` | `Human (postediting)`. |
| `pseudo_ref` | `PseudoRef`, the pseudo-reference. |
| `challenge_hyp` | A challenge-set hypothesis such as `FECE_hyp1`. |

### Missing values

Every column may be null; the description of each column says when. A run that does not cover an item has no rows for it (there are no null rows), and a run that makes no prediction for a task has null in that task's columns. Text values are copied exactly from the source data: nothing is trimmed, re-cased or clipped.

### Language codes found in challenge-set ids

Two-letter and locale codes occur only in the ids of the challenge sets. The mapping below was chosen by the release builders, not by the organisers: the script or variant behind a bare code (`zh` as Simplified Chinese, `ar` as Standard Arabic) is an assumption.

| code in the id | normalised |
| --- | --- |
| `en` | `eng_Latn` |
| `de` | `deu_Latn` |
| `de_DE` | `deu_Latn` |
| `cs` | `ces_Latn` |
| `uk` | `ukr_Cyrl` |
| `ar` | `arb_Arab` |
| `el` | `ell_Grek` |
| `is` | `isl_Latn` |
| `ru` | `rus_Cyrl` |
| `hi` | `hin_Deva` |
| `ja` | `jpn_Jpan` |
| `ja_JP` | `jpn_Jpan` |
| `ko` | `kor_Hang` |
| `zh` | `zho_Hans` |
| `zh_CN` | `zho_Hans` |

## `items`

One row per test item.

| column | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item_id` | `string` | Unique identifier of the test item: six fields (collection, source language, target language, domain or challenge-set name, document, paragraph or segment) joined by `_###_`. |
| `collection` | `string` | Either `official` for the main test set or `challenge` for a challenge set. |
| `challenge_set` | `string` | Name of the challenge set the item belongs to (`GAMBITP`, `FECE`, `QEbreak`, `AGGREE`, `LIGATUR`, `RefQuality-PD` or `RefQuality-PE`), or null for official items. |
| `domain` | `string` | Text domain (`news`, `social`, `speech`, `software`, `edu` or `factchecking`) for official and RefQuality items, or null for every other challenge item. |
| `src_lang` | `string` | Source language, normalised to a three-letter language code, a script and, where needed, a region (for example `eng_Latn` or `zho_Hant_TW`). |
| `tgt_lang` | `string` | Target language, normalised to a three-letter language code, a script and, where needed, a region (for example `deu_Latn` or `zho_Hans`). |
| `src_lang_orig` | `string` | Source language code exactly as it is written in `item_id` (for example `en` or `eng_Latn`). |
| `tgt_lang_orig` | `string` | Target language code exactly as it is written in `item_id` (for example `de_DE` or `deu_Latn`). |
| `lp` | `string` | Language pair as a short `src-tgt` code, such as `ces-deu` or `eng-zho_CN`. |
| `is_priority` | `bool` | True for official items whose language pair is one of the eight priority directions, and false for every other item, challenge items included. |
| `doc_id` | `string` | Identifier of the source document the item belongs to, the fifth field of `item_id`. |
| `para_idx` | `int32` | Zero-based index of the paragraph within its document, taken from the last field of `item_id`, and null for FECE and QEbreak, whose item ids end in a segment hash. |
| `src` | `string` | Source text of the item, exactly as in the test set. |
| `ref_text` | `string` | Reference translation, exactly as in the test set, or null when the item has no reference. |
| `ref_type` | `string` | How the reference was produced: `native` (human translation from scratch), `postedit` (post-edited machine translation), `pseudo` (machine-generated pseudo-reference), `unknown` (a reference text is present but its type is not recorded) or `none` (no reference text). |
| `ref_type_orig` | `string` | Reference type exactly as recorded in the source data (`human`, `postedit`, `pseudo` or `undefined`), or null when the data records no type. |
| `asr` | `string` | Automatic speech recognition transcript of the source audio, present for speech items only. |
| `video_path` | `string` | Relative path of the source video file as recorded in the test set, present for speech items only. |
| `screenshot_path` | `string` | Relative path of the screenshot of the original post, present for some social media items only. |
| `n_systems` | `int32` | Number of systems (machine translation, human translation, pseudo-reference or challenge hypothesis) that have a hypothesis for the item. |

## `pairs`

One row per item and MT system.

| column | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item_id` | `string` | Unique identifier of the test item: six fields (collection, source language, target language, domain or challenge-set name, document, paragraph or segment) joined by `_###_`. |
| `collection` | `string` | Either `official` for the main test set or `challenge` for a challenge set. |
| `challenge_set` | `string` | Name of the challenge set the item belongs to (`GAMBITP`, `FECE`, `QEbreak`, `AGGREE`, `LIGATUR`, `RefQuality-PD` or `RefQuality-PE`), or null for official items. |
| `domain` | `string` | Text domain (`news`, `social`, `speech`, `software`, `edu` or `factchecking`) for official and RefQuality items, or null for every other challenge item. |
| `src_lang` | `string` | Source language, normalised to a three-letter language code, a script and, where needed, a region (for example `eng_Latn` or `zho_Hant_TW`). |
| `tgt_lang` | `string` | Target language, normalised to a three-letter language code, a script and, where needed, a region (for example `deu_Latn` or `zho_Hans`). |
| `src_lang_orig` | `string` | Source language code exactly as it is written in `item_id` (for example `en` or `eng_Latn`). |
| `tgt_lang_orig` | `string` | Target language code exactly as it is written in `item_id` (for example `de_DE` or `deu_Latn`). |
| `lp` | `string` | Language pair as a short `src-tgt` code, such as `ces-deu` or `eng-zho_CN`. |
| `is_priority` | `bool` | True for official items whose language pair is one of the eight priority directions, and false for every other item, challenge items included. |
| `doc_id` | `string` | Identifier of the source document the item belongs to, the fifth field of `item_id`. |
| `para_idx` | `int32` | Zero-based index of the paragraph within its document, taken from the last field of `item_id`, and null for FECE and QEbreak, whose item ids end in a segment hash. |
| `system` | `string` | Name of the system that produced the hypothesis, exactly as in the source data. |
| `system_type` | `string` | Kind of system: `mt`, `human_scratch`, `human_postedit`, `pseudo_ref` or `challenge_hyp`. |
| `src` | `string` | Source text of the item, exactly as in the test set. |
| `hyp` | `string` | Hypothesis translation, exactly as in the source data, including empty and whitespace-only outputs. |
| `ref_text` | `string` | Reference translation, exactly as in the test set, or null when the item has no reference. |
| `ref_type` | `string` | How the reference was produced: `native` (human translation from scratch), `postedit` (post-edited machine translation), `pseudo` (machine-generated pseudo-reference), `unknown` (a reference text is present but its type is not recorded) or `none` (no reference text). |
| `is_reference_candidate` | `bool` | True when the hypothesis equals the reference apart from surrounding whitespace, so that it may be a copy of the reference; it marks the reference itself (a `human_scratch`, `human_postedit` or `pseudo_ref` row) and also any MT output or challenge hypothesis that equals it, so filter on `system_type` to tell them apart. |
| `hyp_is_empty` | `bool` | True when the hypothesis is empty or contains only whitespace. |

## `submissions`

One row per participant run, item and system.

| column | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run_id` | `string` | Identifier of the evaluator run: the numeric submission id, or the name of the organisers' baseline (for example `gemma_ref` or `872013`). |
| `task` | `string` | Task the run was entered for: `task1` (error spans, with Task 2 scores as well for the organisers' Task 1 baselines), `task2` (segment scores) or `task3` (error-free judgements). |
| `item_id` | `string` | Unique identifier of the test item: six fields (collection, source language, target language, domain or challenge-set name, document, paragraph or segment) joined by `_###_`. |
| `lp` | `string` | Language pair as a short `src-tgt` code, such as `ces-deu` or `eng-zho_CN`. |
| `system` | `string` | Name of the system that produced the hypothesis, exactly as in the source data. |
| `t1_errors` | `list<struct<start: int32, end: int32, severity: string, category: string>>` | Task 1 error spans the run predicts for the translation, each with `start` and `end` offsets into the hypothesis, a `severity` and a `category` (which may be null), or null where the run makes no Task 1 prediction for the row. |
| `t1_omission` | `string` | Omission severity (`minor` or `major`) that the run predicts for the translation, or null when it predicts no omission or makes no Task 1 prediction. |
| `t1_instruction_fault` | `string` | Instruction fault that the run reports for the translation, or null when it reports none or makes no Task 1 prediction (null in every row of this release). |
| `t2_score` | `float64` | Task 2 quality score the run predicts for the translation, copied unchanged from the source (some runs score below 0 or above 100), or null where the run makes no Task 2 prediction. |
| `t3_error_free` | `bool` | Task 3 judgement that the translation is free of errors, or null where the run makes no Task 3 prediction. |

## `baselines`

One row per organiser baseline run, item and system.

| column | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run_id` | `string` | Identifier of the evaluator run: the numeric submission id, or the name of the organisers' baseline (for example `gemma_ref` or `872013`). |
| `task` | `string` | Task the run was entered for: `task1` (error spans, with Task 2 scores as well for the organisers' Task 1 baselines), `task2` (segment scores) or `task3` (error-free judgements). |
| `item_id` | `string` | Unique identifier of the test item: six fields (collection, source language, target language, domain or challenge-set name, document, paragraph or segment) joined by `_###_`. |
| `lp` | `string` | Language pair as a short `src-tgt` code, such as `ces-deu` or `eng-zho_CN`. |
| `system` | `string` | Name of the system that produced the hypothesis, exactly as in the source data. |
| `t1_errors` | `list<struct<start: int32, end: int32, severity: string, category: string>>` | Task 1 error spans the run predicts for the translation, each with `start` and `end` offsets into the hypothesis, a `severity` and a `category` (which may be null), or null where the run makes no Task 1 prediction for the row. |
| `t1_omission` | `string` | Omission severity (`minor` or `major`) that the run predicts for the translation, or null when it predicts no omission or makes no Task 1 prediction. |
| `t1_instruction_fault` | `string` | Instruction fault that the run reports for the translation, or null when it reports none or makes no Task 1 prediction (null in every row of this release). |
| `t2_score` | `float64` | Task 2 quality score the run predicts for the translation, copied unchanged from the source (some runs score below 0 or above 100), or null where the run makes no Task 2 prediction. |
| `t3_error_free` | `bool` | Task 3 judgement that the translation is free of errors, or null where the run makes no Task 3 prediction. |
| `variant` | `string` | Snapshot of the baseline: `official` for the released predictions, or `alt` for the original predictions from before deduplication, with Task 1 fields only; the label is provisional, as it follows decision A1 and will be confirmed against the paper in v1.0. |

## `systems`

One row per official evaluator run.

| column | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run_id` | `string` | Identifier of the evaluator run: the numeric submission id, or the name of the organisers' baseline (for example `gemma_ref` or `872013`). |
| `name` | `string` | Name the team gave the submission in its model card, followed by the run id in brackets where several runs share that name, so that every name is unique. |
| `canonical_name` | `string` | Name under which the findings paper lists the system, curated by the organisers and never suffixed with the run id. |
| `org` | `string` | Organisation or organisations that entered the run, as written in the model card. |
| `description` | `string` | Short free-text description of the system, copied from the model card. |
| `reference_usage` | `string` | Free-text account of which kinds of reference translation the system uses and how, copied from the model card. |
| `model_size` | `string` | Size of the model behind the system, as the team wrote it in the model card. |
| `closed_model_name` | `string` | Name of the closed-source model the system calls, as written in the model card. |
| `api_provider` | `string` | Provider or host of the API through which the closed-source model is called, as written in the model card. |
| `link` | `string` | Link to the submitted system that the team volunteered for publication in its model card, or an empty string where it gave none. |
| `underlying_model` | `string` | Model or models behind the system as the findings paper reports them, curated by the organisers (`—` for the metrics that use no model, and `not stated in the paper` where the paper gives none). |
| `paper_citation` | `string` | Citation of the paper that describes the system, in the author-year form of the findings paper, or `[Citation missing]` where the findings paper has none. |
| `is_baseline` | `bool` | True for the organisers' baselines and false for participant submissions. |
| `uses_reference` | `bool` | True when the model card says that the system uses the provided reference translations, false when it says that it does not, and null when the answer is missing or is neither yes nor no. |
| `ensemble` | `bool` | True when the model card says that the system is an ensemble, false when it says that it is not, and null when the answer is missing or is neither yes nor no. |
| `fine_tuned` | `bool` | True when the model card says that the team fine-tuned its model, false when it says that it did not, and null when the answer is missing or is neither yes nor no. |
| `open_weight` | `bool` | True when the model card says that the system is based on open-weight models, false when it says that it is not, and null when the answer is missing or is neither yes nor no. |
| `open_source` | `bool` | True when the model card says that the submitted system is open-source, false when it says that it is not, and null when the answer is missing or is neither yes nor no. |
| `threshold_inclusive` | `bool` | True when a Task 2 score equal to `t3_threshold` counts as error-free, false when only a higher score does, and null when the model card says neither or both. |
| `allow_t1_to_t2` | `bool` | True when the team allows the organisers to convert its Task 1 output into a Task 2 prediction automatically, false when it does not, and null when the model card gives no readable answer. |
| `allow_t1_to_t3` | `bool` | True when the team allows the organisers to convert its Task 1 output into a Task 3 prediction automatically, false when it does not, and null when the model card gives no readable answer. |
| `allow_t2_to_t3` | `bool` | True when the team allows the organisers to convert its Task 2 output into a Task 3 prediction automatically, false when it does not, and null when the model card gives no readable answer. |
| `covers_all_priority` | `bool` | True when the run has at least one row for every one of the eight priority language pairs among the official items. |
| `t3_threshold` | `float64` | Task 2 score that separates the team's Task 2 predictions that are converted to error-free judgements from those that are not: a higher score counts as error-free, and a score equal to the threshold does so when `threshold_inclusive` is true. Null where the model card gives no numeric threshold. |
| `tasks` | `list<string>` | Tasks the run has predictions for: the one task of a submission, `task1` and `task2` for the organisers' Task 1 baselines, and `task2` for the seven sentence-level metric baselines. |
| `lps` | `list<string>` | Language pairs, as short codes sorted alphabetically, in which the run has at least one row, challenge sets included. |
| `n_items` | `int64` | Number of distinct test items for which the run has at least one row. |
| `n_pairs` | `int64` | Number of rows (one per item and system) that the run has in its prediction table. |

## `mt_systems`

One row per MT system.

| column | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `system` | `string` | Name of the system that produced the hypothesis, exactly as in the source data. |
| `system_type` | `string` | Kind of system: `mt`, `human_scratch`, `human_postedit`, `pseudo_ref` or `challenge_hyp`. |
| `n_items` | `int64` | Number of distinct test items for which the system has a hypothesis. |
| `lps` | `list<string>` | Language pairs, as short codes sorted alphabetically, in which the system has hypotheses. |

## `challenge_sets`

One row per challenge set.

| column | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | Name of the challenge set, as in the `challenge_set` column of `items` and `pairs`. |
| `full_name` | `string` | Title of the paper that introduced the challenge set, copied from the reference list of the findings paper, or a descriptive name for the organisers' reference-swap sets, which have no published title. |
| `authors` | `string` | Authors of the challenge set, as in the reference list of the findings paper. |
| `citation` | `string` | Citation of the paper that describes the challenge set, in the author-year form of the findings paper. |
| `what_it_tests` | `string` | Short description of the phenomenon that the challenge set probes, from the findings paper. |
| `hyp_semantics` | `string` | What the hypotheses of the set are, and which `system` names they appear under, or `not stated in the paper` where the paper does not say. |
| `ref_semantics` | `string` | What the reference of the set is, or `not stated in the paper` where the paper does not say. |
| `lps` | `list<string>` | Language pairs, as short codes sorted alphabetically, in which the set has items. |
| `n_items` | `int64` | Number of distinct items in the challenge set. |
| `n_pairs` | `int64` | Number of rows (one per item and system) that the challenge set has in `pairs`. |

## `grand`

The organisers' lossless archive of the shared task, kept unchanged next to the typed configs
(`wmt26-grand.parquet`, one row per test item). Its columns are `item_id` and `src` (text);
`ref`, `hyps` and `resources` (JSON); `ground_truth__record` (JSON), the raw human-annotation
records; one JSON column for each submission and each baseline snapshot, named by the
`grand_column` of [`data/MANIFEST.tsv`](../data/MANIFEST.tsv); and `source_provenance` (JSON), the
source file and line behind every column of the row. Source files with identical content are
stored once: `canonical_column` in the manifest names the column that holds them, and
`__item_fields__` stands for the five item columns. Loading the file needs `datasets>=4.7.0`,
which reads the JSON columns as dicts. The baseline diagnostic `stage1_finish_reason`, which some
baseline runs record, is dropped from the typed configs and appears only in this config.
